title: Candidate feedback draft - Ralph Mendoza (SWE Platform)
ratings: coding:4 - good problem solving, a bit slow on edge cases
system_design:3 - solid high-level, some gaps on operations/scale
domain_infra:4 - strong infra knowledge, previous distributed cache work
culture_fit:4 - aligns with runbook + ops-first mindset
content:
Quick notes from 2026-03-10 interviews (panel loop)

Summary:
- Candidate: Ralph Mendoza — 7+ years infra/platform experience, last 3 yrs at mid-size infra SaaS (k8s + cache + feature flags). Applied for Senior SWE (Platform).
- Interview vibe: calm, pragmatic. Good trade-off thinking.
- Comp expectation: voiced 160-180k base + equity expectation in band that aligns with senior level (ask recruiting to confirm).

Strengths:
- Deep practical experience with distributed caches and stateful service scaling. Gave nice anecdotes about cache invalidation, warming strategies, and TTL tuning.
- Ops-minded: has on-call & postmortem ownership stories; drove runbook improvements at previous company.
- Debugging: strong root cause analysis approach; used metrics + lightweight tracing to narrow down perf regressions.

Concerns / Gaps:
- System design detail level: good high-level designs but weaker on exact traffic shaping and specific request routing under multi-tenant constraints. Struggled with a question about fallback routing when primary model is overloaded (couldn't propose a low-latency consistent approach quickly).
- Coding speed: solved the prompt correctly but was slower than expected; missed a couple of corner-case tests (concurrency scenario). Likely solid with time, but needs pair-programming ramp in first 1-2 months.
- Quantitative tradeoffs: comfortable qualitatively, but when pressed for numeric cost/latency estimates, he hedged. Not a blocker but would benefit from more exposure to cost-modeling exercises.

Detailed interview snippets:
- Coding (Aisha): Medium array + concurrency problem. Ralph implemented a correct approach with locks + sharded state. Missed an edge case for empty input and had off-by-one in one loop. Fixes were straightforward once hinted. Strong test and debugging thinking.
- System design (Priya): Design a low-latency inference routing layer. Ralph proposed a tiered model pool + replica set approach. Good reasoning about capacity and KV cache, but didn't fully specify admission control or graceful degradation when all pools saturated.
- Infra (Elisabeth): Deep about cache eviction policies and compaction; concrete runbook and SLO discussion. Gave examples where he changed eviction heuristics to reduce tail latency.
- Behavioral (Samir): Ownership story about reducing on-call toil; led a small project to automate a PagerDuty playbook. Good cross-team communication examples.

Score breakdown (panel consensus):
- Recommend move to onsite: 3/5 panel vote (Priya hesitant on design depth; others supportive).
- Overall hire level: fits Senior but borderline for Staff. Recommend follow-up interview focusing on: scaled routing/admission control, cost/latency quantification, and one more timed coding exercise.

Suggested next steps / TODOs:
- Recruiting: confirm comp band and counteroffer headroom. (recruiting@)
- Schedule follow-up deep-dive on scaled routing + admission control (Priya to run, 60-75m).
- Quick timed coding (40m) focused on concurrency and edge cases (Aisha volunteer to pair).
- If follow-ups go well -> onsites or loop with infra lead for final sign-off.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Was the candidate's recent role more IC or manager leaning? He said IC but did some team leads; need to confirm scope and direct reports. (ask in follow-up)
- Double-check his familiarity with our stack: k8s operator experience? He mentioned some Helm charts but not operator development.
- Cultural fit looks good; would he be comfortable with our PLG rapid rollout cadence and weekend oncall? He said yes but want more concrete examples in follow-up.

Draft closing recommendation (to iterate with panel):
- "Weak yes" -> move to a targeted follow-up focusing on operational design and a faster-paced coding problem. If follow-ups show more depth on admission control and faster coding, extend an offer at Senior level. If not, consider a no-hire.

Notes for scorecard fields (for Confluence/Jira transfer):
- Technical strengths: infra, cache, ops-mindedness
- Technical risks: design depth for high saturation scenarios, speed under pressure
- Leadership/Communication: high
- Recommendation: follow-up loop (targeted)

-- Jordan
